newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open a bit lower, dollar steady.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open a bit lower, dollar steady.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries opened a bit lower on Wednesday as the dollar steadied.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was off 1/32 to 101-24/32, yielding 6.37 percent in initial trades.

"Treasury prices are slightly lower, dipping overnight with the dollar," said Kim Rupert, senior economist at MMS International. "Most of the activity was concentrated in the five- and 10-year sector."
The market sees a fairly light calendar of new economic data on Wednesday.
At 1000 EST/1500 GMT, the Commerce Department issues figures for October U.S. housing completions, data that are unlikely to affect the market.

Of more import is the Federal Reserve's Beige Book, an anecdotal description of business conditions around the nation. This account is used as a briefing book at the regular meetings of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the monetary policy-making arm of the Federal Reserve.
The Beige Book is rarely at odds with economic data the market has recently gotten so it tends not to move prices.

This time, economists expect the Beige Book to reflect the slower business conditions that prevailed during the third quarter and in the first part of the fourth quarter. A reference to scattered tightness in the labor market would also come as no surprise, given continued moderate levels of new jobless claims.
One item that will attract the market's attention even if prices do not move on it is the release of the Boskin Commission report to the Senate Finance Committee.
The independent commission was appointed by Congress and led by Stanford economist Michael Boskin.

The New York Times reported on Wednesday that the commission will report that the government is overstating the inflation rate by 1.1 percentage points, costing it billions of dollars in inflated Social Security and other benefit payments. The commission will call on Congress and the Clinton Administration to solve the problem. It will not propose a specific plan for dealing with the political opposition to any step that would rein in benefits like Social Security. But it will recommend that Congress and the Administration take a variety of specific, technical steps to revise the index.

Federal funds were trading at 5-7/16 percent, above the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate. Analysts at MMS International predicted that the Fed's open market desk would add temporary reserves to the banking system "with at least a cutsomer repo" and said the chance remained that the Fed would add permanent reserves to the system buy buying coupons.

The market has been anticipating a coupon pass for a couple of weeks. On Tuesday, the market erased early gains in the afternoon when the Fed was again absent from the market during the customary time for conducting such an operation.
In early trade, three-month bill rates were down one basis point to 4.88 percent. Six-month rates were unchanged at 4.99 percent. Year-bill rates were also unchanged at 5.10 percent.

The two-year note was unchanged at 100-1/32, yielding 5.61 percent. Five-year notes were down 1/32 to 100-3/32, yielding 5.85 percent. Ten-year notes were down 2/32 to 103-5/32, yielding 6.07 percent.
